pr_title: server: fix instance IDs for shared-process tenant servers to node IDs
pr_body:
We have a number of callers that assume the node ID and instance ID
can be used interchangably. In shared-process mode, this has revealed
a number of issues that we need to investigate and resolve.

This PR, however, papers over those issues to an extent by allowing
the shared process tenant servers to inherit the node ID from the
server that is starting it. This then ensures that their SQL instance
ID is the same as their node ID.

I've updated some of the names in NodeIDContainer to make the intended
usage more clear.

Fixes #84602

Epic: CRDB-14537

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/96857)

issue_context.title: server: enforce SQL Instance ID = KV node ID for in-memory tenants [CRDB-14537 followup]
issue_context.body:
When running in-process, we'd like the SQL servers to have the same SQL instance ID as the KV node ID, so that distsql planning can continue equating the two.

(NB: we might be able to obviate this idea once distsql planning uses localities properly)

Jira issue: CRDB-17759

Epic CRDB-23559
comments:
We've had a conversation with @knz and @ajwerner about related topics; dump it here.
There are two somewhat inter-related issue that deserve thought for embedded tenants: the instance ID (and the corresponding row in `system.sql_instances`) and the liveness session in `system.sqlliveness`. I think it's worth considering whether embedded tenants need either of these.
For the instance ID, it seems more clear that an instance ID does not need to be allocated in the same way it is in serverless, and it also doesn't need to be linked to a session (since, if we use the node ID, it never expires).
For the liveness session, I, for one, find it appealing to also not give tenant servers their own sessions, and instead have them piggy-back on the host's session. This seems conceptually simpler than the alternative to me - one process, one session as opposed to one process, many sessions independently heartbeated.
One way I hope this could be done is by "simply" handing the tenant servers the system's `sqlliveness.Liveness` instance. I hope that this would make all uses of sessions transparently go to the system's key space.
When thinking about sessions, I think one thing worth considering is what option makes it simpler to customize the behavior of embedded tenants wrt sessions, compared to serveless. For example, in serverless we want the tenant process to shut down when the tenant's session expires (related to #92739). In the embedded case, we probably do not want that.

The above proposal from Andrei is sound under the assumption that all sql servers for a given tenant will be shared-process. If we ever have a mix of some processes which are shared-process and some which are standalone, we'd be in a pickle.

The sqlinstance separation would be ~fine -- the standalone sql servers probably never need to communicate with shared-process tenant servers. It's not perfect though because we use the knowledge of the previous instance in the tenant to do bookkeeping in tenant rate limiting infrastructure (see the discussion of `next_instance_id` [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/docs/RFCS/20210604_distributed_token_bucket.md#system-table)). Maybe shared-process tenants don't use the rate limiting?

The sqlliveness separation would just not work. The standalone instances and embedded instances would be searching in a different universe and would each think the other's sessions were not live.

nit: let's scratch the word "embedded". The word is "shared-process servers" vs "standalone servers".

Agreed that Andrei's approach does not support mixed deployments. That is fine for now. We'll document this restriction. If/when we need more, we can start reserving rows in the liveness table for the (pre-allocated) node IDs, so they don't get reused by instance ID allocation. We can think about this at a later stage.
I edited the above comment to match the desired terminology.
